beforeImage.subsector: Wireless towers and edge digital infrastructure
beforeImage.description: Mexico Telecom Partners owns and operates wireless communications infrastructure in Mexico, with activities centered on towers and adjacent digital infrastructure. Its customers include major wireless carriers and other communications users that require shared infrastructure for coverage, densification, and network expansion. The operating model is asset-heavy and lease driven, supported by long-lived telecom sites and recurring tenancy revenue rather than consumer retail billing. DigitalBridge and company materials describe MTP as one of the largest private tower companies in Mexico, founded in 2014, with operations across the country and additional activity in edge data centers. MTP was created in 2014 with the backing of DigitalBridge and Macquarie, and the current ownership percentages between those shareholders are not publicly disclosed.

milestones.event: Macquarie Mexican Infrastructure Fund and Digital Bridge formed Mexico Tower Partners by merging their existing Mexican tower portfolios.
MTP inaugurated a data center in Mexico City.

afterImage.name: Mexico Telecom Partners
aliases: Mexico Tower Partners, S.A.P.I. de C.V.
afterImage.subsector: Wireless towers and edge digital infrastructure
afterImage.description: Mexico Telecom Partners, legally Mexico Tower Partners, S.A.P.I. de C.V., is a neutral Mexican digital-infrastructure platform that owns and operates towers, rooftop sites, distributed antenna systems, small cells, edge facilities and data-center infrastructure. The platform serves major wireless operators and colocation users across Mexico. It was formed in May 2014 by combining Digital Bridge and Macquarie Mexican Infrastructure Fund portfolios. A June 2026 BMV filing reported approximately 3,737 sites and confirmed an unchanged 50/50 ownership split: DigitalBridge through MTP Mexico Holding B.V., and Macquarie Asset Management through MMIT I and MMIT II. The 2022 Macquarie-side transfer was internal, InfraBridge is not a direct owner, and no signed or closed direct platform sale was identified through August 19, 2026.

milestones.event: The 50/50 Digital Bridge and Macquarie Mexican Infrastructure Fund combination closed to form Mexico Tower Partners; the transaction was announced the following day.
Macquarie transferred its MTP shares and related loans internally to MMIT I and MMIT II without changing Macquarie's aggregate 50% interest.
